title: When the way is lost
hook: when the great Tao is forgotten, rules about kindness and duty appear (Tao Te Ching 18)

segments.voice: Yesterday, we did it ourselves: the best leaders are barely noticed. Your line was they did it themselves. Did you help someone and let them keep the whole of it? Day one thousand eighty.

A sign taped to an office fridge: please label your food. Below it, a second sign: please don't take food that isn't yours. Below that, in red: whoever is eating my yogurt, stop. Nobody wrote those signs on day one. On day one, people just didn't take each other's lunches. Each sign marks the spot where something was already lost. Chapter eighteen of the Tao Te Ching is only a few lines long, and it reads every sign like that one: as the mark of something already lost.
screen: `PLEASE LABEL YOUR FOOD.` → `WHOEVER IS EATING MY YOGURT, STOP.` → `EACH SIGN MARKS A LOSS.`

segments.voice: First, the opening line. When the great Way is abandoned, the chapter says, kindness and righteousness appear. That sounds backward. Aren't kindness and doing right good things? They are. The chapter's point is about when people start talking about them. On this reading, no one needs speeches about kindness where kindness is simply how things are. The speeches start once it's gone missing. Second, the pattern repeats. When cleverness and know-how show up, great pretending follows. When families fall out of harmony, people start praising devoted children and loving parents. When a country falls into disorder, loyal ministers get noticed. Each virtue becomes visible, and gets a name and a rule, at the moment its absence is felt. Third, who's listening. Kindness and righteousness, ren and yi, are words the school of Confucius treasured, and some readers hear this chapter as part of a conversation between the two schools. Confucian teachers have their own answer: that naming and practicing virtue is how people grow into it. The Tao Te Ching's line is that the naming comes late. Fourth, the hint inside the chapter. If rules about kindness are a sign the way was lost, then the way itself is something before the rule. Not unkindness, and not a world without rules. A kindness that came first, before anyone needed to write it on the fridge. The question the chapter leaves is whether a person can find their way back to that, one small act at a time.
screen: `THE WAY IS LOST, AND KINDNESS GETS NAMED.` · `EACH VIRTUE SHOWS UP WHEN IT'S MISSED.` · `REN AND YI: A CONVERSATION OF SCHOOLS.` · `SOMETHING BEFORE THE RULE.` · then, large: `BEFORE THE RULE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: be kind without a rule. Settle, and think of one small kindness you could do today that no rule asks of you. Not because it's polite, not because someone's watching, not because you'd feel guilty otherwise. Just because it fits. Refilling the coffee pot. Holding a door a little longer. A message to someone who's been quiet. Hold that one act in mind, and notice whether it feels different from the ones you do because you're supposed to. The bell holds the time.
When the way is lost. Chapter eighteen's warning: the rules about kindness and duty show up after the thing they describe has gone missing. Today's word.
screen: `WHEN THE WAY IS LOST — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: before the rule. Do one kind thing today that nobody asked for and no sign requires, and do it quietly. Day one thousand eighty.

howItsDone: Some readers of the Tao Te Ching use chapter eighteen as a check on themselves: they notice when they do good only because a rule says so, and look for kindness that comes before any rule.

fork.setup: the office fridge has three signs about not taking food. by chapter eighteen's light, what do the signs tell you?
options: the office is very well run.
something was lost before the signs went up.
fork.reveal: when the great Way is abandoned, kindness and righteousness appear. each rule marks a spot where something went missing.

original.note: Chinese: the great Way, the Tao, which chapter eighteen says has been abandoned when kindness and duty get named.

trapdoor: what you thought: when the way is lost means being lost in the woods.
what it means: rules about kindness and duty show up after the kindness itself has gone missing.
what a scholar hears: ren and yi, kindness and righteousness, words prized by the Confucian school; some readers hear the chapter as one side of a conversation.

notes: Chapter 18 paraphrased throughout. Legge 1891's first line ('When the Great Tao ... ceased to be observed, benevolence and righteousness came into vogue') was not quoted because the writer could not confirm every word, including Legge's parenthetical gloss.
Some received texts omit the line about cleverness and great hypocrisy (the writer recalls that the Guodian bamboo version lacks it; verify); the teach includes it as in the received text. Confirm.

The teach names the Confucian school and gives its view fairly ('naming and practicing virtue is how people grow into it'); a scholar of both traditions should check that this is fair and that nothing ranks one school over the other.
The fridge-sign illustration is the writer's, not the text's.

Editor pass: unclear hook line ('reads that list of signs from the bottom up') rewritten; 'nobody gives speeches about kindness' framed as a reading; 'long conversation' (an unsourced time claim) and 'deep answer' (stock) trimmed in teach and trapdoor.
